title: President Trump's Grass Obsession: Why He Can't Stop Talking About Lawns
summary: Have you ever met someone who just can't stop talking about their lawn? Well, President Donald Trump is that person—times a hundred! Since he came back to the White House, he's brought up grass at least 45 times in public. That's about once every 12 days. He even talks about it more than big stuff like the war in Iran or the economy. So what's the deal? Trump says his grass skills come from owning lots of golf courses. 'I know a lot about grass because I own a lot of golf courses,' he said. 'And, if you don't have good grass, you're not in business very long.' He even met with a 'grass nerd' from Scotts Miracle-Gro to plan new lawns. But here's the funny part: while he brags about grass, he's also paving over a lot of it! He covered part of the Rose Garden lawn with a stone patio because women in high heels kept sinking into the mud. 'The women would be lifting up their shoes, saying, You've destroyed my shoes,' he said. And for his 80th birthday, he set up a UFC octagon on the South Lawn, turning big chunks into dusty dirt. Now crews are building a huge helicopter pad, ripping out even more grass. Trump says the new Marine One helicopters are so powerful they tear up the turf. 'When you land on the grass, it's not that the grass gets discolored—it gets ripped out,' he explained. So, is he a grass hero or a grass villain? Either way, he's definitely a grass chatterbox!
why_it_matters: Even small choices like what to do with a lawn can show how someone balances what they say they care about (like grass) with other needs (like not ruining shoes or landing safely).

background_read: The President lives in the White House, which has a famous garden called the Rose Garden (right outside the Oval Office) and a huge grassy area called the South Lawn where helicopters land.
Presidents often make changes to the White House grounds. For example, President Richard Nixon added a bowling alley under the driveway.
The president's helicopter, Marine One, is used for short trips and lands right on the South Lawn so the President can leave quickly.
Article_Structure: WHO: President Donald Trump, a grass expert from Scotts Miracle-Gro, White House ground crews, and people who visit the White House in high heels.
WHAT: Trump talks about grass all the time—at least 45 times—but at the same time his crews are paving over parts of the famous lawns with stone, a fight ring, and a new landing pad.
WHERE: At the White House in Washington, D.C., especially the Rose Garden and South Lawn.

WHY: He says the stone patio stops women's shoes from sinking in mud, the UFC octagon was for his birthday fun, and the helicopter pad is needed because the new Marine One helicopters are so powerful they rip out chunks of grass.

perspectives.description: Trump is a true grass expert. He knows what good grass needs because he owns golf courses, and the stone patio and helicopter pad are smart fixes that save people and machines from getting stuck or damaged.

Behind all the talk, Trump is actually destroying big sections of historic White House lawns. He brags about loving grass but tears it up just for fun events or personal comfort, showing he doesn't really care.
Trump simply talks about grass a lot—more than about serious issues. The changes to the lawns are nothing new; every president adjusts the grounds, but Trump's personality makes it a bigger story.
